passages.LOG-P0345:
XV. Within the framework of contract law, the provision of remedies serves to address the consequences
of a breach, aiming to restore justice to the aggrieved party. The primary and most common remedy is


an award of damages, or monetary compensation. The foundational principle is to protect the innocent
party’s expectation interest—to place them, financially, in the position they would have occupied had
the contract been fully performed. Courts may alternatively award damages based on the reliance
interest (covering wasted expenditure) or the restitution interest (reclaiming a benefit conferred). This
compensation is not unlimited; it is constrained by the rules of remoteness, established in Hadley v
Baxendale, which limits recovery to losses arising naturally from the breach or those within the parties’
contemplation. Furthermore, the claimant has a duty to mitigate their loss, and damages must be proven
with reasonable certainty.
Where damages are deemed an inadequate remedy, equitable remedies may be sought. Specific
performance is a discretionary court order compelling the defaulting party to execute their precise
contractual obligations. It is typically reserved for contracts concerning unique assets, such as land or
rare goods, where monetary compensation cannot substitute the promised performance. Similarly, an
injunction—another discretionary order—commands a party to refrain from a particular action, such as
breaching a negative covenant within the contract. Crucially, both remedies are granted at the court’s
discretion and are not available as of right.
It is essential to distinguish these breach-related remedies from rescission. While not a remedy for
breach per se, rescission is available for vitiating factors like misrepresentation or undue influence. It
operates to set the contract aside ab initio (from the beginning), aiming for restitution and a return of
both parties to their pre-contractual positions. Thus, the landscape of contract remedies offers a tailored
response, from compensatory financial awards to coercive equitable orders, ensuring redress is both
practical and just in light of the breach’s nature and the subject matter of the agreement.
passages.LOG-P0346:
VI. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 recognises acid attack victims as a category of persons entitled to
statutory protection, rehabilitation, and disability-related benefits. In Shaheen Malik v. Union of India & Anr. (2025),
the Supreme Court invoked its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to hold that the expression "acid attack
victim" must receive a purposive and beneficial interpretation. The Court held that the expression includes not only
persons disfigured by the throwing of acid but also persons who are forcibly made to consume acid and those who suffer
internal injuries caused by acid or similar corrosive substances, notwithstanding the absence of visible external
disfigurement. The Court directed that this interpretation shall operate retrospectively from the commencement of the
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and urged the Union Government to suitably amend the Schedule appended
to the Act so as to remove the existing statutory lacuna. The Court observed that the legislative objective of the Act is to


protect every person who suffers disability as a consequence of an acid attack, irrespective of the manner in which the
injury is inflicted.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 criminalises voluntarily causing injury by throwing, administering, or otherwise using
acid or any corrosive or burning substance. The offence includes causing permanent or partial damage, deformity,
maiming, disfigurement, disability, internal injuries, burn injuries, or rendering a person into a permanent vegetative state.
The offence is cognizable and non-bailable and is punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than ten years, which
may extend to imprisonment for life, together with a mandatory fine that is just, reasonable, and payable directly to the
victim for medical treatment and related expenses. Attempt to commit an acid attack constitutes a separate cognizable and
non-bailable offence punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than five years but which may extend to seven
years, together with fine. A public servant who intentionally fails to record information relating to an acid attack commits
a cognizable and non-compoundable offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than six months
but which may extend to two years, in addition to fine.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 guarantees immediate and free medical treatment to every acid attack
survivor. Every public and private hospital is under a statutory obligation to provide prompt treatment without delay or
refusal and must immediately inform the police upon admitting such victim. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita
further provides for a statutory Victim Compensation Scheme under which acid attack survivors are entitled to
compensation independent of, and in addition to, any fine or compensation imposed upon the offender by a criminal court.
Acid attack survivors are also entitled to financial assistance under governmental rehabilitation schemes and to free legal
aid through the District Legal Services Authorities, State Legal Services Authorities, and the National Legal Services
Authority irrespective of their economic status.
Acid attack has been recognised as a specified disability under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
Consequently, acid attack survivors are entitled to all statutory rights, reservations, rehabilitation measures, social security
benefits, and welfare schemes available to persons with disabilities. In Parivartan Kendra v. Union of India (2013), the
Supreme Court directed strict regulation of the manufacture, sale, and distribution of acid and held that the authorities
responsible for regulating its sale must ensure effective implementation of the regulatory framework. The statutory
framework governing acid attacks must therefore be interpreted in a manner that advances the constitutional values of
dignity, equality, rehabilitation, access to justice, and effective protection of victims.

Iran will stop using traditional boats and only use drones from now on.
Global energy prices will become completely stable once the talks finish.
questions.solution: The passage notes that shipping contracts and insurance policies must be redrawn because operators must now sail with the risk of sudden, unannounced closures, which directly implies insurers will price in this heightened uncertainty through higher rates.

questions.questionText:
A scientist argues: “Since life appeared very early on Earth, life must commonly arise on suitable
planets across the universe.” Which of the following best identifies the flaw in this reasoning?
options: It assumes intelligence and simple life must appear through the same process.
It draws a broad cosmic conclusion from one possibly unrepresentative case.
It rejects fossil evidence merely because it cannot confirm alien civilizations.
It treats late intelligence as proof that life itself is biologically impossible.
questions.solution: This option identifies the flaw of hasty generalisation. The scientist moves from one known planetary case to a sweeping conclusion about planets across the universe.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is least likely to follow if the passage’s reasoning about resilience is
sound?
options:
Policymakers may be able to cushion short-run volatility without immediately sacrificing
medium-term growth objectives.

Some adverse impact from the shock is still plausible even if India’s baseline outlook
remains relatively strong.

External constraints can matter less when domestic demand remains a stable driver of
expansion.

Export performance implies trade barriers are largely inconsequential for most sectors
under current conditions.
questions.solution: The passage says exports did better than anticipated despite tariffs, but it does not claim tariffs have little or no impact across most sectors. Better-than-expected performance could result from sectoral shifts, temporary factors, or resilience in specific categories, while other sectors still suffer.

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Courts generally refrain from interfering with delegated legislation in
technical or economic matters.
Reason (R): Courts consider the wisdom of policy choices made by delegated authorities
to be conclusive.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.

questions.questionText:
Which assumption is most necessary for the organiser’s conclusion that the seating arrangement
encouraged wider interaction?
options: Relatives from the same branch usually avoid speaking to each other at family dinners.
Guests mainly interacted with those seated beside them rather than only across the table.
Second cousins are always more likely to talk than first cousins at formal gatherings.
Younger relatives generally create livelier conversations than older relatives at reunions.
questions.solution: This is correct because neighbour-based interaction is essential to the organiser’s explanation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the underlying assumption of the author in the passage?
options:
Indians are willing to modify their traditional dietary preferences if provided with adequate
nutritional information.

The correlation between poor diet quality and NCDs establishes that dietary modifications
can effectively reduce NCD prevalence.

Physical inactivity contributes less significantly to NCDs than dietary factors in the Indian
population.

Whole wheat and millet flour are nutritionally superior to refined cereals in all health
parameters.

The 2026 NDS prescribes focus after critiquing past expansive agendas. For its

options:
Public opinion has turned decisively against foreign interventions of any kind,

Technological advancement alone can now solve security dilemmas previously

All prior administrations knowingly pursued policies that would weaken
              America’s global standing over the long term.

The previous approach actively hampers effectively countering today’s
              primary identified dangers.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is a necessary condition for “No Mow May” to improve native pollinator
nutrition in U.S. lawns?
options: The campaign must be supervised by local councils rather than homeowners.
The lawns must be managed exactly like traditional hay meadows.
The practice must eliminate every non-native plant before flowering begins.
The blooming plants must provide nutrients useful to native pollinators.
questions.solution: The passage’s concern is that flowers in a lawn are not automatically beneficial to native pollinators. For pollinator nutrition to improve, the flowers must contain useful nectar or pollen.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is least likely to be treated as “desire” in the author’s sense?
options: A scholar pursuing a theorem because solving it may bring private satisfaction.
A teenager wanting rare shoes because classmates treat them as prestigious.
An employee seeking promotion after colleagues begin admiring senior positions.
A traveller buying water in extreme heat to prevent collapse during a journey.
questions.solution: This option is least likely to be treated as desire in the author’s sense. The traveller seeks water to prevent physical collapse, which places survival at stake.

questions.questionText: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the author's argument?
options:
Companies in India report unfilled positions requiring technical skills while unemployment
rates among recent graduates remain high.

The number of engineering colleges in India has increased by 40% over the past decade,
producing more graduates annually.

Graduate unemployment rates in India are lower than in several other developing nations
with similar economic growth rates.

Students from top-tier institutions secure employment faster than those from lower-ranked
colleges across all disciplines.
questions.solution: This option directly strengthens the author's main argument by providing evidence of the specific mismatch described. If companies have unfilled positions (indicating job availability) while graduates remain unemployed, this confirms the author's claim that the problem is not a shortage of jobs but rather that graduates lack the skills employers need.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is correct?

The person immediately clockwise of Ovi is Ishan’s first cousin and Rhea’s second cousin once
removed.
The person immediately counterclockwise of Juhi is Ishan’s second cousin.

The person opposite Karan is Ishan’s second cousin and sits immediately counterclockwise of

questions.solution: The Final arrangement: Ishan — Ovi — Karan — Rhea — Lavya — Pranav — Manav — Juhi

questions.questionText: Based on the passage, which of these statements would the author most likely agree with?
options:
A temporary two-week ceasefire is entirely worthless unless it permanently resolves every
underlying conflict immediately.

Intense military strikes can inadvertently strengthen an adversary's regime by making them
more entrenched and resolute.

Applying massive military force against a nation will inevitably compel its leadership to
surrender immediately.

Issuing intimidating threats on social media platforms remains the optimal method to initiate
peace negotiations.
questions.solution: This is a simple summary of the passage's point that the intense "decapitation strategy" only caused the Iranian regime to become further "entrenched" (secure and stubborn).

questions.questionText:
If the passage's overall logic holds true, what is most likely implied about a society that chooses to
reject surveillance?
options: Such a society values individual liberty more than marginal gains in security
It will inevitably experience significantly higher crime rates as a result
It must rely exclusively on traditional human patrols for all policing needs
It can achieve perfect privacy without any inherent trade-offs involved
questions.solution: ; the conclusion frames societal choice as values-driven, where rejecting surveillance reflects prioritizing "autonomy" (liberty) over safety prioritization and its "marginal" benefits.

questions.questionText:
Based on the passage, what is an underlying assumption of the critics' argument regarding
"judicial coherence"?
options: Constitutional interpretation and appellate law often overlap in practical legal disputes.

Legal issues can always be neatly categorized into either "constitutional" or "appellate"
buckets.
The Supreme Court's backlog is primarily caused by complex constitutional litigations.
The Federal Constitutional Court will be superior in rank to the Supreme Court.
questions.solution: ; "conflicting jurisprudence" assumes that the same legal issue might be viewed differently by both courts.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is an assumption that supports the critics’ claim that “flexibility” is a
mirage?
options: Real flexibility requires meaningful choice, not choices shaped by hidden platform controls.
Real flexibility requires workers to work fixed hours under direct human supervision.
Real flexibility requires platforms to offer higher profits to workers than to companies.
Real flexibility requires platforms to eliminate all rules for safety and quality control.
questions.solution: ; if control constrains choices, the flexibility claim becomes hollow as critics argue.

questions.questionText:
Rina, a YouTuber, uses a 15-second ANI news clip in her documentary critiquing

options: Rina’s use is likely fair dealing, as it is transformative and for criticism.
Rina’s use is infringement, since she used more than 10 seconds.

Rina’s use is automatically exempt since it is for current affairs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the author most likely to disagree with?
options: The judiciary has no role in examining the principles underlying property compensation.
Legislative amendments have limited judicial review to an extent in property matters.
The right to property is less contentious than other fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution.
The word "amount" in Article 31(2) fully resolved the conflict between the legislature and judiciary.

commentator's argument.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following exchange. Critic: "Your focus on a physical body is
misplaced. A truly advanced AI, even without a body, could form a self-model based
purely on its interactions with data and users, creating a 'digital' self." The author's
response would most closely align with which counterargument?
options:
That proposal is identical to the current capabilities of large language models, which
show no signs of selfhood.

Such a digital self-model would be irrelevant to understanding the human condition of
selfhood.

A self-model without persistent physical anchoring could not replicate the
fundamental "embodied me" distinction I describe.

Historical philosophy has already disproven the possibility of a self arising from pure
information.

questions.questionText:
Only six roads A, B, C, P, Q and R connect a military camp to the rest of the country. Only one
out of A, P, and R are open at any one time. If B is closed so is Q. Only one of A and B is open
during storms. P is closed during floods. In the context, which one of the following statements
is correct?
options: Under normal conditions only three roads are open.
During storms at least one road is open.
During floods only three roads are open.
During calamities all roads are closed.
questions.solution: During storms: “Only one of A and B is open.” This statement guarantees that at least one among A,B is open (exactly one, in fact). So during storms, at least one road is open.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following would best strengthen the argument that diverse agricultural landscapes
benefit both farmers and the environment?
options: Studies show that monoculture farming leads to reduced soil fertility over time.
Research indicates that diverse cropping systems lead to higher overall income.
Studies show that fields with multiple crops have fewer pest infestations.
Research indicates that organic farming practices increase consumer preference.

questions.questionText: Which of the following identifies the most significant flaw in the author's reasoning in the passage?
options:

modern times, most or all traditional practices can be similarly adapted.

The author argues that technological progress is inherently harmful to cultural heritage without providing
supporting evidence.
The author relies entirely on historical examples while ignoring present-day developments in India.
The author concludes that preserving cultural heritage is impossible in a modern economy.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is most likely to follow if life is easy to form but intelligence is difficult to
evolve?
options: Bayesian models would no longer require any factual inputs.
Alien visitors must have avoided leaving physical evidence on Earth.
Earth’s fossil record would become irrelevant to cosmic probability.
Many planets may contain organisms without producing reflective civilizations.
questions.solution: This option follows most strongly from the stated condition. If life forms easily, many planets may develop organisms.

questions.questionText: Which of the following must necessarily be false if the passage is true?
options:
Conflict over valued opportunities may persist even when institutions publicly praise
cooperation.
Some people may still succeed on merit even in a society shaped by structural competition.

Once social roles are efficiently distributed, conflict theory would treat competition as
largely avoidable.

People in power may influence outcomes in ways that weaken a purely merit-based account
of success.
questions.solution: the passage presents conflict as unavoidable within and between social groups. So even if social roles were distributed efficiently, the theory would not treat competition as largely avoidable.

defensible conclusion based on the passage?
options: The regulation is valid because environmental protection is a legitimate objective.

The regulation is invalid because courts can assess the wisdom of environmental
poicy.
The regulation may be invalid due to excessive delegation and unfettered discretion.

The regulation is valid because delegated legislation enjoys absolute presumption of
validity.


                                  LOGICAL REASONING

questions.questionText:
Which of the following, if true, would most WEAKEN the argument that formalizing India's e-waste
recycling sector will significantly reduce environmental harm?
options:
Most informal recyclers already follow safety protocols comparable to those used in formal recycling
facilities worldwide.

The carbon emissions from manufacturing new electronics have decreased by 40% since 2010 due to
improved production methods.

Consumers in India are increasingly choosing to repair their devices rather than replace them with
new models.

Formal recycling facilities in neighbouring countries have successfully reduced heavy metal
contamination by 75% over five years.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is the most likely outcome of ecologists using “function” without
engaging with philosophical debates about the term?
options: Philosophers may replace field research with abstract theories about environmental loss.
Biodiversity studies may become irrelevant once species richness is no longer central.
Public concern may decline because technical words rarely influence ordinary thinking.
Ecological claims may carry hidden assumptions that scientists have not fully examined.
questions.solution: the author worries that ecologists use the word “function” without examining its deeper meaning. If a scientific term carries an unnoticed idea of purpose, it may influence how ecological loss is understood.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the suggestion that the CJP could translate
into meaningful political change in India?
options: The CJP surpassed the BJP's Instagram following within one week of its creation.

Abhijeet Dipke has stated publicly that the CJP does not intend to contest any elections or
transform into a formal political party.

Opposition leaders who endorsed the CJP belong to parties that have struggled to win
elections against the BJP in recent years.
A survey found that 29% of young Indians avoid political engagement altogether.
questions.solution: The question asks what would most weaken the prospect of tangible political change. Option (a) is about social media metrics — impressive, but the passage itself notes that surpassing the BJP's Instagram following has not yet translated into ground-level political change.

questions.questionText: Which of the following arguments most closely parallels the reasoning style in the passage?
options:
Since some communities value cooperation, competitive markets must be a cultural
misunderstanding rather than a structural phenomenon.

Because a policy is widely taught, it must be accurate, and any criticism of it is necessarily
ill-informed.

Because prestigious grants are limited and selection panels protect their influence, awards
often reflect entrenched advantage rather than pure merit.

Since resources are scarce, fairness is impossible, so all allocation systems are equally
unjust in practice.
questions.solution: This follows the passage’s pattern: scarcity creates competition, and gatekeepers preserve advantage, so outcomes need not track merit. It keeps the same causal structure while shifting domains.

questions.questionText: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the RBI’s claim that India is in a “Goldilocks phase”?
options: Several Indian exporters continue experiencing difficulties because of persistent disruptions within international trade markets.
Advanced economies worldwide are witnessing prolonged recessions caused by increasing geopolitical uncertainty and tensions.
Consumer inflation has remained consistently below the RBI’s target range during recent financial quarters.
Domestic equity markets have experienced moderate volatility following fluctuations in global commodity price movements.
questions.solution: Applying all the stated constraints and eliminating inconsistent alternatives leaves Consumer inflation has remained consistently below the RBI’s target range during recent financial quarters. Therefore option C is the only result consistent with the arrangement.

questions.questionText:
In light of the author’s view that price signals are becoming corrupted, which of the following
is least likely to be accepted by the author?
options: Prices usually preserve useful economic signals despite periods of narrative enthusiasm.

Valuations can reward coordinated expectations before present output becomes sufficiently
visible.

Earlier market booms often used persuasive forecasts about coming technological
transformation.
Public exposure may make contested financial stories harder to reverse politically.
questions.solution: This option conflicts with the author’s view of contemporary price signals. The passage states that price is becoming less informative and that market signals are becoming corrupted.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the author’s reliance on old recordings to
study the development of the Kiwi accent?
options: The public lectures attracted audiences interested in unusual vowel patterns.
The early families often shifted between rural districts over several decades.
The recorded speakers were chosen for formal diction rather than everyday speech.
The schools corrected written grammar more often than spoken pronunciation.
questions.solution: This option raises a serious problem for the author’s evidence because formal diction may not reflect ordinary speech. If the recorded speakers were selected for polished pronunciation, their voices may not represent how people commonly spoke.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is least likely to be accepted by the author as a fair implication of the
passage?
options:
Disrupting the sleep cycle may matter medically because the same internal system
regulates multiple bodily functions.

Short-term public safety effects can arise when biological timing and social schedules
become newly misaligned.

Since many people recover quickly, the author’s concerns probably apply only to unusually
fragile individuals.

Adjustment measures may work best when they respond to light exposure rather than
relying on clocks alone.
questions.solution: This option is least acceptable because it shrinks the problem to a narrow minority, whereas the passage treats the issue as socially and medically broader. The author notes that some people may adjust without much trouble, yet still emphasizes widespread sleep deprivation and population-level increases in serious outcomes.

questions.questionText:
Which hypothetical U.S. action would most clearly contradict the 2026 NDS
      principle of prioritization and ending free-riding?
options:
Launching a new open-ended, U.S.-funded global initiative to combat
              corruption in 100 nations.

Demanding higher host-nation support payments for troop deployments as a
              condition for treaty renewal.

Redirecting naval assets from worldwide patrols to concentrate exercises in a
                  single strategic region.

Publicly ranking state adversaries and cyber threats in a tiered list to guide
                  intelligence allocation.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the claim that garlic could deter disease-
spreading insects through the same biological basis?
options:
Old folklore often connects garlic with creatures imagined as blood-feeding nocturnal
threats.

Aedes mosquitoes spread diseases, making inexpensive prevention attractive to public
health authorities.
Mosquitoes sense garlic yet mate normally after relocating to untreated nearby areas.

Garlic sprays remain cheaper than synthetic products in several mosquito-affected regions
worldwide.
questions.solution: This option weakens the reasoning because the passage relies on the idea that sensing garlic may help deter disease-spreading insects. If mosquitoes sense garlic but still continue mating after moving elsewhere, the receptor’s presence would not be enough for pest control.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: E and B purchased a chocolate of same variety.
A and E purchased a chocolate of same variety.
A and B purchased a chocolate of same variety.
D and E purchased a chocolate of same variety.
questions.solution: Applying all the stated constraints and eliminating inconsistent alternatives leaves D and E purchased a chocolate of same variety. Therefore option D is the only result consistent with the arrangement.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the author’s criticism of governmental
disregard?
options: Political leaders praised multilingual education after the circular attracted public attention.
Schools received audited staffing plans, textbooks, and transition modules before the circular.
Some parents prefer Indian languages over foreign languages for cultural reasons.
The Court scheduled hearings after refusing immediate suspension of the circular.
questions.solution: This option most effectively weakens the author’s criticism. If schools had already received staffing plans, textbooks, and transition modules, the allegation of casual implementation becomes less persuasive.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an assumption on which the conclusion of the author depends?
options: Farmers will adopt biodiversity-friendly practices if they see some practical benefits.
Organic farming methods are less practical for most farmers than diverse cropping.
The decline in biodiversity is primarily due to conventional farming practices.
Government regulations are necessary to enforce biodiversity-friendly farming.

questions.questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that which one of the following is most likely true?
options: Germany's annual working hours per worker declined amid rising GDP per capita.
China's population growth fully accounts for overtaking Germany.
Germany's native population has declined over the past 25 years.
India's GDP growth threatens Germany's third-place ranking soon.
questions.solution: Why (A) is right: The passage explicitly says the chart shows that as Germany became more prosperous (higher GDP per capita), annual working hours per worker dropped sharply. Choice (A) is basically a clean re-statement of that sentence, so it must be true.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is not a least likely outcome of the logistical concerns raised by school
administrators?
options: Students may receive uneven instruction despite facing one uniform curricular mandate.
Courts may deem language learning unconstitutional despite no such passage claim.

Foreign languages may become compulsory alternatives despite policy preferring Indian
languages.
Parliament may convert executive policy into legislation whenever schools face shortages.
questions.solution: “Students may receive uneven instruction despite facing one uniform curricular mandate” This follows directly. If some schools lack teachers/textbooks while others have them, instruction quality will be uneven even though CBSE rule is same for all.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following would best strengthen the author's claim that Earth's axial tilt is the
primary cause of seasons?
options: Solar output remains constant while Earth's orbital speed fluctuates slightly.
Regions tilted away receive lower solar angles and shorter daylight durations.
Weather variations in the tropics remain unaffected by planetary orientation.
Solar flares do not align with seasonal patterns in either hemisphere.
questions.solution: This option reinforces the argument by describing the mechanism through which axial tilt influences solar intensity and day length. These changes contribute directly to seasonal variations and thus support the central claim of the passage.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is a necessary assumption behind the idea that “money becomes
control”?
options: Future-based valuation is invalid unless it reflects only present physical assets.

Concentrated capital can influence policy environments that later validate its
expectations.
Predicting distant outcomes accurately requires governments to ignore market pressure.
Public institutions lose all authority whenever private investors become wealthy.
questions.solution: The relevant fact or inference in the passage corresponds to Concentrated capital can influence policy environments that later validate its expectations. Therefore option B is the answer identified by the official key.

questions.questionText:
Suppose a study finds that institutional investors improve housing
        affordability by increasing supply. This finding would most directly:
options:
Strengthen the rationale behind the UK Labour party's approach and its partnership
with firms.
Undermine the economic argument for Trump's executive order.

Challenge the author's claim that rent prices have jumped due to institutional investors
and their market practices.

Explain why the US political unity on this issue is so remarkable and historically
unprecedented.

questions.questionText: All of the following can reasonably be inferred from the passage, except:
options: Material procurement for the ornament may have extended beyond the tomb’s region.
Non-local feathers prove direct diplomatic contact between Chu and foreign courts.
Bird identification can reveal exchange patterns even without direct trade records.
The ornament’s composition may reflect both availability and elite acquisition capacity.
questions.solution: This option cannot be reasonably inferred because it makes a much stronger claim than the passage supports. Possible long-distance trade does not prove diplomatic contact with foreign courts.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is/are assumptions underlying the argument made in the passage?
I. Warning signs emerging from clearly flawed trial runs are sufficient grounds for halting
full deployment.
II. A reliable evaluation system is a fundamental prerequisite for maintaining the overall
credibility of examinations.
III. The outgoing CBSE chairman was personally and directly responsible for ignoring critical
warnings about malfunction.
IV. Students affected by altered grades deserve remedial action beyond mere administrative
transfers and inquiry orders.
V. Digital on-screen evaluation systems are inherently less reliable than traditional manual
methods for high-stakes examinations.
options: Iand II only
III and V only
I, II and IV only
II and V only
questions.solution: Passage Explanation -— 3: The author argues that the government's administrative response, though belated, confirms a serious institutional failure that has compromised examination credibility. His premises are: warnings about the digital evaluation system were raised after a flawed January trial run yet were deliberately ignored; subsequent malfunctions altered grades and produced technical failures at scale; and students bore the consequences of this negligence.

questions.questionText:
The argument that "Gen Z has given up on traditional political parties and wants to create its
own political front in a language they understand" rests on which of the following
assumptions?
options:
Gen Z in India is incapable of understanding or participating in the organisational
structures of traditional political parties.

The language and culture of internet-native political expression is meaningfully different
from that of established parties, and young people find the former more accessible and
representative of their experience.

Traditional political parties in India have deliberately excluded young people from their
leadership structures to protect the interests of older voters.

The CJP will eventually contest elections and displace the BJP and Congress as India's
dominant political forces.
questions.solution: Dipke's argument is that Gen Z wants to communicate politics in "a language they understand" — implying a mismatch between the cultural language of established parties and that of internet-native youth. This is Assumption (b).

questions.questionText:
Which argument has the most similar logical structure to the passage’s claim that entering a
shock “from a position of strength” makes better outcomes more likely, though not certain?
options:
A firm posted record profits last year, so it will certainly beat rivals this year even if costs
surge.

A household has savings, stable income, and low debt, so it will likely handle a sudden
expense better than peers.

A city faced few storms recently, so it will probably avoid flood damage even without
upgrades to drainage.

A country signed one trade pact, so it cannot be harmed by supply disruptions in global
shipping lanes.
questions.solution: This mirrors the passage’s structure by combining buffers with a probabilistic conclusion about handling a shock better than comparable peers. Savings, stable income, and low debt function like reserves, fiscal space, and low inflation as cushions during stress.

questions.questionText: Consider these two statements drawn from the passage: Statement 1: Technologies that claim to advance freedom while actually robbing people of autonomy are existential traps. Statement 2: Many aspects of Big Tech's promised technologies have arguably robbed people of their autonomy. Which conclusion follows most logically?
options: All Big Tech companies are secretly controlled by unelected oligarchs wielding unchecked institutional power.
Many of Big Tech's promised technologies may therefore constitute an existential trap for humanity.
Technologies that genuinely advance quality of life necessarily compromise individual autonomy in some way.

questions.questionText:
A Statement is given followed by two Conclusions numbered I and II. Consider the Statement and
the Conclusions.
Statement: India is the world's largest producer of milk.
Conclusion-I: India is the world's largest exporter of milk.
Conclusion-II: India does not import milk.
Which one of the following is correct?

Neither Conclusion-I nor Conclusion-II logically follows from the statement.
Only Conclusion-I logically follows from the provided given statement.
Only Conclusion-II logically follows from the provided given statement.
questions.solution: In logical reasoning, you cannot deduce external facts from a limited statement. Producing the most milk does not automatically mean a country exports the most (it might consume it all domestically), nor does it mean the country imports nothing (it might import specific dairy variants).

incompetent to contract, the bank refuses. Aman tells the banker, ‘Give him the money. If he does

minor), and the lending bank.

incapacity to enter into financial agreements.
questions.solution: Why B is correct: For a contract of guarantee to exist under Section 126, there must be a valid, enforceable primary debt owed by a principal debtor. Since a minor's agreement is void from the very beginning under Indian law, Kabir cannot owe a legal debt.

Based only on the author's statement that “No one else can do our introspection for us,” and the
author’s argument about the necessity of personal reflection in leadership, which of the following would
the author be most likely to agree with?
options: External advice and mentorship are unnecessary for a leader, as true guidance comes only from within.

Leaders should primarily focus on their external strategies and objectives, as personal introspection can be
misleading.
The role of a leader is to inspire others to introspect, rather than focusing on their own personal reflection.

A leader's ability to self-reflect and understand themselves is crucial for authentic leadership and vision
realization.

questions.questionText:
Speaker A: The collapse of institutional gatekeepers means political debate is now
       driven by engagement metrics, which often amplify extreme voices.

Speaker B: While extreme voices get attention, traditional parties like Labour still shape
policy through sensible, non-inflammatory means that ignore online trends.

On the basis of the passage, what point is most likely agreed upon by both speakers?
options:
Online platforms have definitively replaced traditional broadcasters as the main arena for
political discussion and policymaking influence.

Nigel Farage is demonstrably more effective at digital communication than Keir Starmer,
as shown by comparative follower counts.

Extreme voices now have a larger platform than before due to digital media structures and
incentives.

Focus group-vetted political messaging is now completely ineffective and is universally
mocked online as a primary strategy.

questions.questionText:
A micro-lending NGO disbursed a loan to a woman entrepreneur, Ms. Kavita, based on a verbal
statement by her neighbour, Mr. Gopal, who said at the time of disbursement: She is reliable, you
can trust her. No formal agreement was entered into with Mr. Gopal, no consideration was given to
him, and he made no promise to repay if Kavita defaulted. Kavita later failed to repay. The NGO
sought to hold Mr. Gopal liable. Which of the following correctly analyses the situation?
options:
Mr. Gopal is liable as a surety because his statement at the time of disbursement implied a
guarantee.
Mr. Gopal is liable because oral guarantees are valid under the Indian Contract Act.

Mr. Gopal is not liable because, a guarantee requires an explicit promise to discharge the
principal debtor's liability on default.

Mr. Gopal is liable under a contract of indemnity as his statement caused the NGO to part with
money.
questions.solution: Why A is Incorrect — A statement of trust or reliability does not imply a guarantee in law. Implication of a guarantee requires that the substance of what was communicated amounts to a promise to discharge the debtor's obligation upon default.

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, the colonial perception that semi-arid Indian landscapes were
"degraded" systems rested on all of the following EXCEPT:
options: The visible presence of pastoralists grazing their herds across these landscapes.
The practice of setting dry-season fires to encourage fresh grass growth.
The lower rainfall levels and aridity of the Deccan and interior peninsula regions.

The assumption that in the absence of human activity, these lands would have developed
into closed forests.
questions.solution: Difficulty: Moderate Why C is correct: The passage attributes the "degraded" perception specifically to visible human activity — grazing and fire-setting — and the assumption of suppressed forest potential. Aridity is mentioned separately, in the context of western grasslands being "too arid to support trees," as a distinct ecological recognition — not as a basis for the degradation label applied to the Deccan.

questions.questionText:
"In order to carry out these tasks effectively, the Army needs to have a certain level of manpower."
Which of the following fall closest to the underlying assumption in the given statement?
options: The Indian Army is currently fully staffed and has no shortage of personnel.
The challenges facing the Indian Army are primarily due to a lack of funding and resources.
The Indian Army's ability to carry out its tasks effectively is dependent on having adequate manpower.
The Indian Army's current structure and deployment patterns are sufficient to meet the challenges it is facing.

questions.questionText:
Rajiv, a prominent businessman, decides to retire and transfer ownership of his lucrative chain of
retail stores to his nephew, Karan. However, Karan was recently declared insolvent due to a series of
failed personal investments. Despite his financial insolvency, Rajiv proceeds with the transfer, believing
that Karan’s new control over the retail business would enable him to settle his debts and restore his
financial standing. Rajiv and Karan enter into a formal property transfer agreement. Shortly thereafter,
a creditor of Karan challenges the transfer in court, claiming that Karan's insolvency disqualifies him
from acquiring new assets. Is the transfer of property from Rajiv to Karan valid considering Karan's
declared insolvency?
options:
Yes, because the transfer was made to help Karan settle his existing debts, which aligns with the purpose of
insolvency laws to rehabilitate the debtor.

No, because an insolvent person is disqualified by law from acquiring new assets until they are discharged
from insolvency.

Yes, because Rajiv, as the owner of the property, has the right to transfer his assets to anyone he chooses,
regardless of the recipient's legal status.

No, because the property transfer to an insolvent person requires court approval, which was not obtained in
this scenario.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

Statement 1: The RBI's upward revision of growth forecast and downward revision of
inflation forecast unambiguously indicate that the Indian economy has achieved an optimal
macroeconomic balance.

Statement 2: A nominal growth rate falling below budgetary targets while real growth
remains above potential automatically ensures adequate fiscal space for government
expenditure.

Which of the following statements will the author most likely not agree with?
options: Only Statement 1
Only Statement 2
Both Statement 1 and Statement 2
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2

questions.questionText: Suppose a state government redesigns its welfare system by replacing direct cash transfers and distribution of consumer goods with universal access to high-quality public schooling, healthcare, and employment guarantees. Which of the following would the author most likely infer?
options: Such a redesign would restore the alignment between welfare policy and the classical model of capability-building and public provisioning.
This approach would reduce the political appeal of welfare by eliminating visible and targeted benefits to specific voter groups.
The shift would be largely symbolic since all welfare models ultimately function through redistribution of state resources.
This redesign would intensify citizens' dependence on the state by expanding institutional control over welfare delivery.
questions.solution: Applying all the stated constraints and eliminating inconsistent alternatives leaves Such a redesign would restore the alignment between welfare policy and the classical model of capability-building and public provisioning. Therefore option A is the only result consistent with the arrangement.

questions.questionText:
A enters into an arrangement with B and C in the following terms:
B agrees with C that if A fails to deliver machinery to C as per a separate supply agreement
between A and C, B will “take full responsibility for all losses suffered by C due to such non-
performance and directly compensate C without requiring C to proceed against A.” The agreement
further states that B’s liability “shall arise immediately upon C suffering loss due to A’s failure.”
C subsequently enters into the supply contract with A relying on B’s assurance. A fails to deliver
the machinery. C directly sues B without initiating any action against A.
B argues that since A is the party in breach, the relationship between A and C must first be
enforced, and only thereafter can B’s liability arise.
Now, determine the legal nature of the relationship between A and C (ONLY A-C
relationship).
options: None

It is a contract of guarantee because A is the principal debtor and C is the creditor under a
secured arrangement.
It is a contract of indemnity because B’s obligation depends on loss caused by A’s breach.

It is a contract of guarantee because B’s liability confirms the existence of a surety relationship
between A and C.
questions.solution: Applying all the stated constraints and eliminating inconsistent alternatives leaves None. Therefore option A is the only result consistent with the arrangement.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

Statement 1: The expansion of human settlements into buffer zones is the primary driver of
human-wildlife conflict in Kerala.
Statement 2: Transferring the power to declare animals as vermin from the Centre to the State
will eliminate opacity in wildlife governance.

Which of the following statements would the author most likely not agree with?
options:
Statement 1 identifies a contributing factor while Statement 2 overlooks
              institutional design flaws that transcend jurisdiction.

Both statements correctly identify core issues addressed by Kerala's legislative
              amendment.

Statement 1 reflects a pattern the author acknowledges while Statement 2
              assumes a solution the author questions.

Neither statement captures the author's view that non-lethal interventions
              should precede any declarations of vermin status.

questions.questionText: The author would most likely agree with each of the following statements EXCEPT:
options:
International interdependence through trade creates both economic benefits and vulnerabilities to
regional conflicts that can have global consequences.

Fundamental equality can be achieved more effectively through shared cultural experiences than
through formal institutional policies emphasizing differences.

The regional distribution of professional talents in India represents immutable characteristics that
should guide workforce allocation policies.

Cultural unifying factors can coexist with regional diversity without requiring homogenization of
all populations within a nation.

questions.questionText:
The passage argues that FRS significantly aids criminal investigations. Each of the following,
if true, would weaken this argument EXCEPT:
options:
A large share of the 10,000 photographs uploaded in 2024 belonged to individuals never
subsequently spotted by any camera in the network.

The FRS software carries a documented false-positive rate of 30%, routinely flagging
ordinary commuters as suspects under surveillance.

Processing 10,000 photographs overloads the system's capacity, causing critical alert
notifications to be delayed by up to 48 hours.

In over 80% of FRS-assisted cases, the suspect had already been identified through
conventional means before any FRS match was made.
questions.solution: Why A is correct (does NOT weaken): The official anticipates exactly this scenario — the system is built for suspects not yet spotted. Many undetected individuals simply reflects the system's intended purpose, not a flaw in its design.

questions.questionText:
L was charged with the criminal misappropriation of property offense. The judge experienced a heart
attack while the trial was still going on, and he passed away instantaneously. As a result, the case was still
pending. The plaintiff N brought a new lawsuit against L. L used the res judicata defence to avoid taking
culpability, arguing that he could not undergo another trial. What do you think of L's claim?
options:
According to the principle of res judicata, no one may be punished twice for the same offense; hence L's
claims are true.

The claims made by L are untrue since the circumstances of this case do not fall under the threshold of res
judicata.
Because the lawsuit is meant to be dismissed when a standing judge passes away, L's claims are true.

Since N is free to file the complaint as many times as he wants, L's claims are unfounded. L has no influence
over this.

questions.questionText:
Sanjay, a successful businessman, devises a plan to evade substantial amounts of taxes by transferring
multiple properties to his associates, Amit and Priya. These transfers are documented as legitimate sales
but are in reality part of an elaborate scheme to temporarily shift ownership until after the tax
assessment period, at which point the properties would be transferred back to Sanjay. The properties
involved are valuable commercial lands in a rapidly developing area. However, a government watchdog
catches wind of this unusual transaction pattern and investigates. The investigation reveals the true
purpose behind the transfers, leading to legal action against Sanjay, Amit, and Priya for tax evasion. Are
the property transfers between Sanjay, Amit, and Priya valid?
options:
No, because the transfers were intended for an unlawful purpose, making them void as they are fraudulent
and opposed to public policy.
Yes, because the transfers were documented correctly and signed by all parties, making them legally binding.

Yes, because there is no explicit evidence that the properties will not be transferred back to Sanjay after the
tax assessment period.

No, because the properties in question are in a rapidly developing area, which requires additional scrutiny
under tax laws.

questions.questionText: The author states in the passage: "Many aspects of the technology that Big Tech promised would advance the quality of our lives has arguably turned out to be a grand illusion and an existential trap, perpetrated by an out-of-control combination of government and corporate interests and a few unelected oligarchs that no one or no institution can seem to contain." Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the above statement?
options: Multiple independent regulatory bodies across nations have successfully imposed binding limits on Big Tech oligarchs.
Government agencies frequently collaborate with Big Tech corporations to expand surveillance of ordinary citizens.
The promises made by Big Tech companies in the 1990s were never formally documented in any legal agreement.
Several science fiction authors of the 1980s accurately predicted the monopolistic consolidation of corporate technology power.
questions.solution: Applying all the stated constraints and eliminating inconsistent alternatives leaves Multiple independent regulatory bodies across nations have successfully imposed binding limits on Big Tech oligarchs. Therefore option A is the only result consistent with the arrangement.

questions.questionText:
A manufacturing company, X Corp, wants to buy raw materials from a supplier. Because X Corp
has a poor credit rating, its parent company, Y Ltd, executes an agreement with the supplier which
states: In consideration of you supplying materials to X Corp, Y Ltd acts as a principal obligor and
agrees to pay you for any loss or unrecovered dues resulting from your dealings with X Corp. When
bills go unpaid, the supplier sues Y Ltd directly without suing X Corp first. Y Ltd argues they are a
mere surety and cannot be sued until X Corp is targeted. Decide based on the passage.
options:
Y Ltd’s claim is valid because a surety's liability is always secondary and dependent on a prior
lawsuit against the principal debtor.

Y Ltd’s claim is invalid because the contract is a contract of indemnity in substance; by acting
as a principal obligor, Y Ltd assumed primary, independent liability.

Y Ltd’s claim is invalid because a contract of guarantee allows the creditor to choose whom to
sue, meaning it remains a guarantee but with shared primary status.

Y Ltd’s claim is valid because a contract of indemnity can only exist if the loss is caused solely
by the conduct of the promisor himself.
questions.solution: Why B is correct: By explicitly signing as a principal obligor tasked with protecting the supplier against loss or unrecovered dues, Y Ltd did not take on the secondary, conditional mantle of a surety. Instead, they took on primary liability.

questions.questionText:
Consider the Statement: "Infrasound, those subterranean frequencies produced by ageing
systems of heat and ventilation, assumes a life of its own when ambient noise dies down."
Which of the following can be inferred?
Inferences:
I. Infrasound becomes perceptible to the human mind only during periods of ambient silence.
II. Ageing heating and ventilation systems are the producers of infrasound frequencies.
III. The mind actively attempts to assign meaning to frequencies it cannot consciously identify.
IV. Infrasound-generated unease is experienced identically by all people regardless of their
disposition.
options: Only I and ITI follow from the given statement about infrasound's perceptual conditions.
Only I, I, and IV follow while III does not logically follow at all.
Only II and IV follow while I and III cannot be conclusively inferred here.
Only I, I, and III follow while IV does not logically follow at all.
questions.solution: Only I, II, and III follow while IV does not logically follow at all. This option is correct.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following, if true, would weaken the argument made in the passage except?
I. Leading nutritional scientists globally advise against daily egg consumption citing
elevated cholesterol and significant cardiovascular risk factors.
II. Surveys across diverse Indian households consistently show eggs serve as the single most
affordable complete protein available.
III. Davidson's dietary claims are widely endorsed by multiple certified nutritionists and
public health professionals across India.
IV. Government nutrition programs in over fifteen Indian states specifically recommend eggs
for addressing childhood protein deficiency.
options: IL and IV only
I and III only
All of the above
None of the above
questions.solution: Passage Explanation — 5: The author argues that Davidson's condemnation of eggs as the worst daily food is both scientifically unfounded and culturally exclusionary. His premises are: the claim elevates one dietary tradition over others, reflecting majoritarian bias; eggs serve as an affordable, nutritionally essential protein and B12 source for millions of households; India's food landscape is irreducibly diverse; and sweeping dietary pronouncements ignore empirical evidence.

questions.questionText:
A farmer breached a contract to deliver a common variety of wheat to a bakery on a specific
    date. The bakery was forced to shut down for a day, losing a full day's profits, and incurred
    significant extra costs to source emergency supplies from a distant mill. The farmer was
    unaware of the bakery's specific operational details. In the bakery's suit for breach, which of
    the following losses is most likely recoverable based on the rule of remoteness?
options:
Both the lost profits from the shutdown and the extra supply costs, as all losses were a
             direct consequence of the non-delivery.

Only the extra supply costs, as this loss arises naturally from such a breach, unlike the
             specific lost profits.

Only the difference between the contract price and the higher market price for the
             wheat on the date it should have been delivered.

Neither type of loss is recoverable because they were not within the contemplation of
             the parties at the time they made the contract.


                                          Logical Reasoning

questions.questionText:
Which of the following would strengthen the argument that humans possess no predetermined
mating script and must consciously work at dating?
I. Evolutionary psychologists confirm human courtship rituals vary drastically across
cultures, unlike fixed instinctual mating displays observed in most animal species.
II. Surveys show daters spend considerable time strategically curating profiles and messages,
revealing deliberate effort rather than spontaneous, instinct-driven behaviour.
III. Psychological studies reveal that daters frequently experience anxiety, hesitation, and self-
doubt, indicating an absence of any instinctive certainty guiding courtship.
IV. Neuroscientists find human dating triggers the same brain reward circuits activated in
other mammals' mating displays, suggesting evolutionary continuity underlies attraction.
options: I, III and IV only
II, II and IV only
I, II and III only
I, Land IV only
questions.solution: "I, II and III only" (The correct answer — precisely reflecting the passage's documented contrast between animals' fixed instinctual mating scripts and humans' conscious, exhausting, script-less effort, since I, I], and III each independently reinforce a distinct dimension of this absence of instinct while excluding IV, which alone asserts the instinctive continuity the passage explicitly denies). The passage explicitly frames animal courtship as instinct-driven and "predetermined," against whic

questions.questionText:
Late at night, Rohan sustained extensive burn injuries when an unidentified assailant threw a corrosive
substance at him outside a railway station. Passers-by immediately shifted him to a nearby private hospital. The
casualty department refused to begin treatment until his family deposited ₹4,00,000 as advance charges and
insisted that the police first complete all medico-legal formalities. As a result of the delay, Rohan's condition
deteriorated significantly. He approached the court alleging violation of his legal rights. Decide the case.
options:
The hospital is not liable because private hospitals may refuse treatment until advance payment and police formalities
are completed.

The hospital is liable because all hospitals are legally required to provide immediate and free treatment to acid attack
victims without procedural delay.

The hospital is not liable because only government hospitals are obligated to provide free treatment to victims of acid
attacks.
The hospital is liable only if Rohan proves that the corrosive substance caused permanent disfigurement.

questions.questionText:
After surviving a corrosive substance attack by an unknown assailant, Kavya was left with permanent
locomotor impairment and reduced functional capacity in one arm. Following her recovery, she applied for


rehabilitation assistance, skill development support, and financial benefits under government welfare schemes
meant for persons with disabilities. The authorities rejected her application, stating that acid attack survivors are
not covered under disability-related welfare schemes unless separately recognised under a different statutory
category. Kavya challenged the decision before the appropriate authority. Decide the case.
options:
Kavya is not eligible for disability-based schemes because acid attack survivors are excluded unless separately certified
under each welfare scheme.
Kavya is eligible for disability-based schemes because acid attack has been included in the list of disabilities.

Kavya is eligible only for medical compensation schemes and not for disability-related welfare benefits unless a court
specifically directs otherwise.

Kavya is not eligible because disability benefits apply only to congenital disabilities and not to injuries arising from
violent acts.
